item.title: AI-First Ideas Get Redone Until They Scale
item.description: Founders discuss why promising AI products may require multiple attempts to reach market scale.
item.content:encoded:
Founders discuss why promising AI products may require multiple attempts to reach market scale.

Original source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VhR2Sh6rbmM

Digg story: https://digg.com/tech/t2n6c3e1

Hiten Shah posted on X that models keep improving and builders' understanding grows, so a strong AI-first idea without enough users or market saturation will be recreated by others until it reaches scale. Jane Manchun Wong quoted the remark with a note emoji. Shah followed up to correct the phrasing from "scales" to "scale" while confirming the intent. The three-post exchange on X centers on this pattern of repeated attempts for promising but under-adopted AI products.

item.title: OpenAI Ends Cursor Access After SpaceX Acquisition
item.description: Cursor's founder confirms OpenAI will end direct model access after the acquisition.
item.content:encoded:
Cursor's founder confirms OpenAI will end direct model access after the acquisition.

Original source: https://openai.com/index/our-decision-on-cursor-following-its-acquisition-by-spacex/

Digg story: https://digg.com/tech/cpbd83av

OpenAI announced it will terminate Cursor's direct access to its models following the coding tool's acquisition by SpaceX. The change takes effect in three months. Cursor co-founder and CEO Michael Truell stated that OpenAI models currently handle about 5 percent of user traffic and said the company is speaking with OpenAI to resolve the issue. Cursor was an early user of OpenAI models. Observers including Miles Brundage and Matthew Berman linked the decision to concerns over SpaceX and Elon Musk. Amjad Masad of Replit offered free OpenAI model access on its platform as an alternative.
